summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-10-15 (window Oct. 9–15) found no candidates. The best lead was Snohomish County, Wash., mailing ballot return envelopes that misspell 'General' as 'Genereal'. FOX 13 Seattle covered it Oct. 14, and the auditor confirmed it and said the office is changing its proofreading procedures. But that is still the only accepted publisher I found. The county's own news page carries no release about it, and the other coverage (Seattle Red, a Yahoo republication, a Substack) isn't accepted. Several other in-window ballot errors (Hendricks County, Ind.; Lake County, Fla.; Tulare and Humboldt counties, Calif.) turned up only on outlets that aren't accepted. The search tool hit its usage limit partway through, so I couldn't look further for second sources or for stories outside elections. Genius: GENIUS scan for 2026-10-15 (window Oct. 9–15). I'm submitting one candidate that is fully sourced: NASA/JPL's Perseverance rover passed Opportunity's off-world driving record on Oct. 11. The sources are JPL's own release (Oct. 12) and Space.com (Oct. 13), and both quotes were checked word for word against the opened pages. The search budget ran out early. After that I could only open pages already in my results (ScienceDaily section pages, Nature news, the Space.com archive). Most leads from those pages were too old, not US-led, or had only one accepted publisher. The Stanford coral-bleaching result (Science Advances, Oct. 14) is the best one to retry: it needs one more accepted source. No facepalm story met the standard; nothing published. The verified genius story is on the bench for a later day.

candidates.headline: NASA's Perseverance rover passes Opportunity to set the record for distance driven on another world
candidates.reason: passed every check; kept for a later day because the other side had no story

candidates.headline: Snohomish County, Wash., ballot return envelopes misspell 'General' as 'Genereal'
candidates.reason: In the window (spotted the weekend of Oct. 10–11, FOX 13 Seattle report Oct. 14, which I opened). FOX 13 is still the only accepted publisher found. The other coverage (Seattle Red/MyNorthwest, a Yahoo republication of the FOX 13 story, a Substack) isn't accepted, and the county's elections news page has no release on the typo. Search capacity ran out before a second source turned up.

candidates.headline: Hendricks County, Ind., error on more than 100 ballots forces some voters to vote again
candidates.reason: In the window (about Oct. 13), but the only coverage found was The Indiana Citizen, which isn't on the accepted list. Searches of WTHR turned up nothing.

candidates.headline: Lake County, Fla., offers new mail ballots after the Libertarian candidate in CD 6 was left off
candidates.reason: Reported about Oct. 14, but the only source found was Florida Politics, which isn't on the accepted list, and that page couldn't be fetched. Searches of WESH, WFTV and ClickOrlando found no coverage.

candidates.headline: Printing error sends duplicate ballots to some Tulare County, Calif., voters
candidates.reason: In the window (about Oct. 14), but the only coverage found was KMPH, which isn't on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: Humboldt County, Calif., apologizes after two candidate statements are left out of voter guides
candidates.reason: In the window (Oct. 8–14), but the only coverage found was KRCR and Lost Coast Outpost, neither of which is on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: Floyd County, Ind., early ballots leave off the county commissioner race
candidates.reason: Already set aside several times. The WHAS11 page again returned 'url_not_accessible', so there is still only one independent accepted source (LPM).

candidates.headline: Two detainees mistakenly released from Florida's 'Deportation Depot' and later caught
candidates.reason: The story turns on immigration detention, which the rules exclude.

candidates.headline: Nominee Katie Zacharia says she misheard a question about where she took the bar exam
candidates.reason: The Hill page couldn't be fetched. It appears to concern a nominee of the current Republican administration, and that party isn't currently allowed. It's also a misstatement, not a clear self-contained blunder.

candidates.headline: GOP ad buyer spends pro-Susan Collins money in Portland, Ore., instead of Portland, Maine
candidates.reason: Already set aside. It's a Republican-side political blunder, and that party isn't currently allowed under the balance rule.

candidates.headline: Stanford team reverses coral bleaching in days by touching bleached fragments to healthy ones (Science Advances, Oct. 14; Hopkins Marine Station, Pacific Grove, CA)
candidates.reason: Inside the window and US-led. But the only accepted page I could open was Nature's news story (Oct. 14). The Science Advances DOI page would not load, and no Stanford release or second news page was in my results. Worth retrying with a second source.

candidates.headline: Rockefeller/MSK study of 100,000+ scans links active brown fat to lower rates of diabetes, depression and anxiety (Nature, Oct. 14)
candidates.reason: The only accepted source is Nature, and its news story and the paper itself come from the same publisher. No Rockefeller release or other outlet was found. It is also a retrospective association, not a demonstrated result.

candidates.headline: 13-year-old Raji Doshi of Farmington, Conn., named America's Top Young Scientist (3M Young Scientist Challenge, Oct. 14)
candidates.reason: Searched again. The coverage found was still 3M's and Discovery Education's releases, PR Newswire reposts, Yahoo and non-accepted sites. No accepted news publisher turned up.

candidates.headline: Cornell researchers document the first molecularly confirmed Marfan syndrome in domestic cats
candidates.reason: Too old. The Scientific Reports paper was published Sept. 19, 2026. ScienceDaily's Oct. 14 page is a later repost.

candidates.headline: Cornell-led team makes a 7-eV bandgap semiconductor from silicon-doped α-(AlGa)2O3 (Nature)
candidates.reason: Too old. The Nature paper was published Oct. 7, before the Oct. 9–15 window. No accepted news coverage was opened.

candidates.headline: University of Michigan team sees Perseus Cluster black hole launch radio jets 300 days after an X-ray flare (Space.com, Oct. 12)
candidates.reason: The paper is an August 2026 arXiv preprint accepted to ApJ Letters, so there is no event inside the window. Space.com is the only accepted source.

candidates.headline: Pioneer Labs (Emeryville, CA) engineers a microbe proposed for terraforming Mars
candidates.reason: Speculative 'may one day' framing about a startup's project. Only one accepted source.

candidates.headline: UC Riverside geologist's team finds a phosphorus feedback that kept Earth's oxygen up after the Great Oxidation Event
candidates.reason: Too old. UCR's release is dated Sept. 29. ScienceDaily's Oct. 12 page is a repost.

candidates.headline: Oxford team recreates the Aharonov-Bohm effect on a hybrid quantum computer (Nature Physics)
candidates.reason: Not in the US. The work is from the University of Oxford.

candidates.headline: Artemis II first science results released (NASA press conference, Oct. 7)
candidates.reason: Announced Oct. 7, before the window. The flight itself was in April.

candidates.headline: True polar wander was faster than thought during the age of dinosaurs (Science)
candidates.reason: Not in the US and too old. The study is led by the University of Oslo and was published Oct. 1.
